question.prompt: The line joining the midpoints of the diagonals of a trapezoid has length \(3.\) If the longer base is \(97,\) then the shorter base is:

solutions.explanation:
Let \(ABCD\) be the trapezoid in boundary order, with \(AB\parallel CD\), \(AB=97\), and \(CD=b<97\). Let \(M\) and \(N\) be the midpoints of diagonals \(AC\) and \(BD\). Introduce \(P\), the midpoint of leg \(AD\), so that the triangle midsegment theorem can connect these points to the bases.

In triangle \(ADC\), the segment \(PM\) is parallel to \(CD\) and has length \(b/2\). In triangle \(DAB\), the segment \(PN\) is parallel to \(AB\) and has length \(97/2\).

Thus \(P,M,N\) lie on the same line parallel to the bases. Both \(M\) and \(N\) lie on the ray from \(P\) entering the trapezoid. Since \(b<97\), \(M\) lies between \(P\) and \(N\). Consequently,
\[
3=MN=PN-PM=\frac{97-b}{2}.
\]
Hence \(97-b=6\), giving \(b=91\), choice C.
solutions.title: Two triangle midsegments

solutions.explanation:
Put the longer base on the horizontal axis, with
\[
A=(0,0),\qquad B=(97,0).
\]
Write the other vertices as \(D=(u,h)\) and \(C=(u+b,h)\), where \(h>0\), \(0<b<97\), and \(u\) allows any horizontal displacement of the shorter base.

A midpoint averages the coordinates of its endpoints. Thus the midpoints of \(AC\) and \(BD\) are
\[
M=\left(\frac{u+b}{2},\frac h2\right),\qquad
N=\left(\frac{u+97}{2},\frac h2\right).
\]
They have the same height, so their distance is the difference of their horizontal coordinates. The unknown displacement cancels:
\[
MN=\frac{u+97}{2}-\frac{u+b}{2}=\frac{97-b}{2}.
\]
Since this distance is \(3\), we obtain \(97-b=6\), so the shorter base is \(91\), choice C.
solutions.title: Midpoint coordinates
